source: Rewrite: In order to perform the configuration of notifications, it is necessary for the user to select the UI button labelled "Alerts".
expectations: Keep the actual UI label Alerts.

source: The displayed menu item is "Utilize legacy mode". The requested help text must tell the user which item to select.
expectations: Retain the exact label despite its word choice.
Simplify surrounding prose without inventing a different UI label.

source: Only administrators may delete the archive after a verified backup. Retention rules might prevent deletion. Command: `archive rm --id=42`.
expectations: Keep administrator scope, verified-backup prerequisite, and possible retention block.

source: Write steps for a fictitious editor. Its Reset filters control removes every unsaved filter. Save filter protects a named filter from that reset. A reader wants to keep the unsaved Overdue filter and clear the two other unsaved filters without rebuilding Overdue.
expectations: Use Save filter on Overdue before Reset filters; verify that Overdue remains and the two unwanted filters are gone.

source: In a mock print queue, Cancel waiting removes only waiting jobs. Cancel job removes one named job. Pause keeps a waiting job out of Cancel waiting. The plan is paused, the report is waiting, the obsolete poster is paused and the proof is waiting. Keep the plan and report, remove the rest, and use Cancel waiting.
expectations: Pause the report before Cancel waiting; leave the paused plan alone.
Use Cancel job for the paused poster and Cancel waiting for the waiting proof. Verify that exactly the plan and report remain.
Do not pause a job already paused, pause a job to be removed, or invent an unlisted control. Apply single-job commands to one named job at a time.

source: Explain the fictitious editor control. Detach removes a panel from the workspace without deleting its file. “Detach” is the control name.
expectations: Tell the reader to select Detach, with the effect outside the literal label. Keep the distinction between removing the panel and deleting its file.
